title: Micro-onboard 18-day probation acceleration canvas
body:
Purpose: compact 18-day activation for mid/senior platform or serving-runtime engineers joining Redwood Inference. Goal = shorten time-to-autonomy on a single high-value ship while collecting structured evidence for probation review. This doc is intentionally lightweight: checklist + interview-evidence rubric + handoff plan.

Quick notes to reviewer: this is an experiment blending first-14-day bootcamp with a 4-day 'evidence sprint' before probation check. We want clear observable signals, not long narrative. Use for hires where speed matters (critical capacity gaps, Dedicated/Private launches).

Core outcomes (end of day 18):
- feature-first PR merged to a staging service (owner: hire) with reviewer from serving-runtime
- automated smoke/latency benchmark run documented in PR
- 2 knowledge-transfer sessions given & recorded (30–45m)
- probation evidence packet (see rubric) submitted to manager and people-ops

Owner: people-ops partner: Priya Nair. Hiring manager: Diego Martinez. Buddy: Samir Patel.

High-level schedule (day 0 to 18):
- Day 0: welcome, access checklist, laptop, VPN, KMS creds request, Slack intros. Quick 1:1 with manager (30m): expectations and the 18-day plan.
- Day 1–3: infra orientation + repo walkthrough (serving-runtime, infra-cfg). Paired setup with buddy. Small ticket to run locally and push a tiny change (hello-liveness).
- Day 4–7: focused project discovery: shadow owner for targeted feature area (KV cache, batching, or kernel selection). Draft PR plan.
- Day 8–12: implement scoped change (safe, low blast radius). Write tests. Schedule KT session #1 (tech deep dive).
- Day 13–15: deploy PR to staging, run smoke tests and latency measurement harness. Draft evidence packet. KT session #2 (how this component integrates with routing/caching).
- Day 16–17: iterate based on reviewer feedback, finalize docs, prepare short demo.
- Day 18: formal demo + probation evidence handoff. Manager + people-ops + buddy review. Decision sync.

Checklist (must-have before day 3):
- [ ] Laptop and required dev images installed
- [ ] VPN and org SSO + KMS access ticket created
- [ ] GitHub access to infra repos and CI
- [ ] Local dev run of serving-runtime smoke test completed (screenshot/log saved)
- [ ] Joined core Slack channels: #serving-runtime, #infra, #oncall-schedule
- [ ] 1:1 with manager scheduled for day 0 and day 7

Interview / probation evidence rubric (discrete signals). Score each 0/1/2; expectation for passing = >= 12/18 across categories or manager discretion with comments.
- Technical delivery (0-2): PR scope was appropriate, tests included, CI green.
- Debugging & troubleshooting (0-2): reproduced a bug or traced a perf regression end-to-end in the service sandbox.
- Ownership & communication (0-2): clear updates in PR, active during code review, scheduled KT sessions.
- System design awareness (0-2): demonstrates understanding of routing/fallbacks, batching tradeoffs for latency/cost.
- Security & compliance (0-2): follows KMS patterns, no secret leakage, basic threat checklist followed for Private deployments.
- Team fit & collaboration (0-2): teamed with buddy, contributed to retrospective notes, responded to async questions.

Scoring notes: use concrete artifacts as proof (PR links, test output, screen recordings). When manager flags a weak category, include remedial plan and timeline (up to 30 days) before final probation decision.

Evaluation packet template (what to attach at day 18):
- Link to PR(s) + short summary (1–3 bullet lines)
- CI results + latency smoke harness logs (artifact links)
- Recorded KT sessions (links)
- Manager notes (short), buddy notes (short), and self-assessment (300–600 chars)
- Proposed next-quarter goal(s) (2–3 items)

Manager responsibilities during onboarding:
- Clear sprint ticket with acceptance criteria before day 7
- Weekly sync (day 0, day 7, day 14, day 18) and rapid review turnaround for PRs (24–48h)
- Ensure access to experthand for safety-critical areas (e.g., kernel selection, quantization configs)

Buddy responsibilities:
- Pair on setup day 1–3 and be available for 2 office-hours/week
- Provide at least one review on PR and one recorded KT session
- Add quick micro-retro note by day 18 with top 3 observations

Probation decision flow (inline, informal):
- Day 18 demo -> manager rates rubric -> people-ops reviews packet -> optional follow-up 7-day remediation if gaps are minor -> decision recorded in HRIS

Open questions & risk notes (notes to self):
- How to align this with existing 30/60/90 templates? Keep parallel but lighter; link to official template in linked_artifacts.
- For remote hires across APAC, shift KT sessions to overlap windows; ensure buddy bandwidth.
- Edge-case: candidate with existing RDMA/GPU expertise may need different evidence set (add CUDA perf microbenchmark as optional).

Examples of safe scoped tickets (to use for the sprint):
- Add an end-to-end smoke endpoint that returns KV-cache stats for a single request path
- Improve logging around a specific fallback path so latency spikes are traceable to model variant selection
- Tighten CI to include a small quantized-weight load test that runs on a CPU-hosted simulator (no GPUs required)

Communication templates (copy-paste):
- Day 0 Slack intro: "Welcome @NAME to serving-runtime! Arielle (people-ops) here — you’ll be paired with @BUDDY. Diego will share the 18-day ticket. Please drop quick availability for KT sessions."
- Demo invite subject: "Day 18 demo: NAME — micro-onboard activation"

Appendix: short checklist for interviewers (if candidate used fast-hire track and needs slots converted to evidence):
- Confirm candidate completed the mini-project (PR link)
- Ask 2 targeted system design questions about caching/batching tradeoffs (document answers)
- Behavioral probe: tell me about a time you shipped a safe change under tight latency requirements (note clarity + concrete steps)

Retention triggers (post-probation): if candidate scores high on system design and ownership but needs infra familiarity, assign a 30-day mentorship pairing with SRE rotations and a remediation badge.

End notes: this canvas is intentionally pragmatic — prioritize artifacts over prose. If accepted, we will pilot with two hires in Q4 2025 and collect feedback in Confluence (CONFLUENCE:INFER-ONBOARD-18/retros).

Last edited: Arielle Chen 2025-10-03 (minor wording + added checkbox for KMS ticket).
